messages:
lenna_support: Heads-up — multiple APAC customers are hitting 502s and long tail timeouts for hosted-inference in asia-southeast (az2). Escalating. Reports started ~09:12 UTC and steadily increased. Customers seeing model requests fail mid-generation.

mike_sre: Seen spikes in 502s on the gateway in that region. Error from gateway logs: `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `502 response` for a subset of upstreams. Can you paste a couple of failing request IDs?

lenna_support: Example request IDs: req_az2_6119, req_az2_6120, req_az2_6127. Customer repro: repeated streaming -> first few tokens then 502. Sample curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"hello"}'` returns 502 in ~4s.

chirag_net: Running tcpdump and iftop on worker nodes in az2. Observed bursts of retransmits and high RTT spikes to upstream model host IPs. Looks like bufferbloat on the provider egress link — long TX queues followed by microbursts.

sara_platform: Traceroute from gateway -> model backends shows intermittent path change after hop 6: `AS12345 -> AS35432` flip with 200-400ms jump, correlated with 5xx spike windows. BGP community updates around the same time reported by our transit provider.

mike_sre: Correlating: gateway 5xx timeline matches provider peering instability windows. Also seeing an increase in connection resets: `RST` and `FIN` in the same traces.

lenna_support: Customers asking for ETA + workaround. We already told them engineers investigating. Anything we can do to reduce impact short-term?

chirag_net: Short term: 1) Route around the affected provider by shifting egress to secondary peer in same AZ. 2) Enable circuit-breaker + retry with exponential backoff at the gateway to avoid hammering problematic upstream. 3) Temporarily increase keepalive and reduce concurrent streams per upstream. I can kick the route change if ops approves.

oncall-bot: Alert: Routing anomalies detected in asia-southeast (az2) between 08:55-09:25 UTC — AS path flaps.

mike_sre: @chirag_net go ahead with route steering to secondary peer for critical inference backend prefixes. Also patch the gateway to set `max_idle=10s` and `conn_pool=50` for those backends. We should add a 2s jittered retry for idempotent requests.

chirag_net: Doing: updating eBGP export policy to prefer peer-B for prefix 203.0.113.0/24, and adding a temporary local route to force egress selection. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: net-policy/az2-route-steer -> canary -> 3 hosts

mike_sre: Also throttling low-priority streaming jobs for az2 to protect control plane. Lenna, coordinate messaging: inform paying customers we've routed around a provider issue and are monitoring.

lenna_support: Sending initial customer note: "We've routed traffic to an alternate provider and applied transient gateway retries; you may see reduced errors as we stabilize. Engineering is monitoring — will follow up in 30m." :thumbsup:

chirag_net: Route change propagated. Early metrics show retransmits dropped ~80% and RTT tail reduced from 450ms to ~70ms. Gateway 502 rate down from 11% to 1.7% in the last 2 minutes.

mike_sre: Nice. Keep watch for flaps. We still need root cause: provider reported bufferbloat due to oversubscription + transient peering queues. We should capture PCAPs for postmortem. Lenna, save the customer repro steps and sample request IDs.

lenna_support: Saved. Also customers asked whether retries will charge them extra tokens — need guidance.

mike_sre: Short answer: retries from our gateway do not re-charge customer tokens because we handle them server-side as part of error mitigation. We need to confirm billing policy with finance before broad comms.

chirag_net: Collected PCAPs and `ss -s` + `netstat -anp` at time of peak. Uploading to /mnt/forensic/az2-bufferbloat/ with filenames pcap-2423456789-0908.pcap and ss-2423456789.log

sara_platform: Noted that failover didn't impact latency for other regions. We should add a policy to prefer multi-homed peers for inference backends by default (postmortem action).

mike_sre: Agreed. Immediate actions: 1) Keep route to peer-B for 1 hour while we observe. 2) Add circuit-breaker rule and retries for streaming endpoints. 3) Notify customers and CS. 4) Collect pcaps/logs + open incident ticket for postmortem.

lenna_support: I'll do the customer follow-up and CC finance on billing note. Any planned rollback?

chirag_net: If peer-B shows any issue, we'll re-evaluate. Rolling back route change is a single policy update. I'll monitor BGP RIB and queue lengths.

mike_sre: Thanks team. Once stabilized, let's run a canary of increased concurrency to ensure no latent issues. Also add an automated runbook step: if retransmit rate > 5% for 3m, auto-steer egress.

lenna_support: Filing incident ticket with summary and attaching logs/snapshots. Will include customer-impact timeline and list of affected request IDs.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2423456789 — Routing-induced bufferbloat causing 5xx/timeouts in asia-southeast (az2). Priority P1.

mike_sre: Closing temporary mitigation when last 15m error rate < 0.5% and RTT p50 < 80ms. Leaving monitoring alerts on. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and provider SLA discussion.

lenna_support: FYI — customers acknowledged the update and saw reduced errors. Will keep thread updated if anything new pops up.

chirag_net: continuing to monitor queues + BGP.

mike_sre: Thanks. Good work triaging and steering.
